decisionQuestion: What single globally deterministic, pre-label rule should replace the unresolved SD7 handling for documents for which the canonical 5-token shingle relation is undefined, while minimising changes to the already-frozen methodology and preserving unbiased SET_P / candidate-independent SET_R?

keyFactAboutDefinedness.statement: R3 SD7 Jaccard is UNDEFINED only when BOTH documents yield no 5-token shingle (empty union, 0/0). When exactly one document is short its shingle set is empty and the other is not, so Jaccard = 0 / |S(long)| = 0: DEFINED, and below 0.90. The canonical implementation withholds every short document from EVERY comparison - more conservative than R3 literally requires - but the only genuinely undefined case in R3 is short-vs-short.
keyFactAboutDefinedness.rImpliedInvariant: For every pair on which R3 is defined, identical canonical normalised token sequences imply identical shingle sets, hence Jaccard 1.0, hence NEAR_DUPLICATE. R3 already treats "identical normalised text" as a near duplicate wherever it can measure it.

A.summary: For a pair on which canonical 5-token comparison is undefined because at least one document has fewer than five canonical tokens, the pair is a near duplicate iff the two COMPLETE canonical normalised token sequences are exactly equal; otherwise not. The >=5-token Jaccard rule is byte-for-byte unchanged.

properties.shortBranchRelationIsAnEquivalence: equality of sequences is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, so short-text components are CLIQUES

smallestDefensibleExtension.argument: Among relations that (i) agree with R3 wherever R3 is defined, (ii) use only the canonical SD7 normalisation, (iii) add no number, and (iv) preserve the invariant R3 already exhibits (identical normalised text => near duplicate), exact sequence equality on the undefined branch is the LEAST relation: (iv) forces every equal pair to be an edge, and nothing in (i)-(iii) licenses any further edge without a new similarity gradation. Always-include adds fewer edges but violates (iv); every other fallback adds a gradation.

B.summary: When 5-grams cannot be formed, shingle with a smaller n and reuse Jaccard >= 0.90.

analysis.howNWouldBeSelected: needs a NEW rule: n = min(5, |T(a)|, |T(b)|) per pair, or n = min(5, |T(d)|) per document, or a fixed fallback n (1, 2 or 3). Each is a separate methodological choice; none is implied by R3.
analysis.thresholdMeaningAcrossN: 0.90 was set (uncalibrated) for 5-grams. At n = 1 Jaccard is token-SET overlap: order and repetition vanish, so different sentences built from the same words collide. At n = 1 or 2 over 1-4 tokens the attainable Jaccard values are a handful of coarse fractions, so 0.90 degenerates to "identical sets" for very short texts and becomes something else at n = 3 or 4. One threshold does not carry one meaning across n.
analysis.emptyText: still undefined at every n (0 tokens => empty set at every n): B does not remove the 0/0 case and would need a further special rule.
analysis.differingDocumentLengths: a per-pair n would re-measure short-vs-long pairs at a smaller n. R3 already DEFINES those pairs (Jaccard 0 at n = 5), so B would CHANGE verdicts R3 has, and could join a short document to a long one.
analysis.calibrationBurden: each n needs its own threshold justification; calibrating on real data would require inspecting the very documents R45 must not inspect, and not calibrating leaves an arbitrary threshold reused out of its domain.
analysis.reproducibility: deterministic once fixed, but the specification has several free choices
analysis.overCollapseRisk: HIGH at n = 1 for very short navigation-like texts that share their tokens in a different order
analysis.methodologyComplexity: HIGH: a metric family, a selection rule for n, and an empty-text rule
arbitraryNewNumericChoices: the fallback n (or the n-selection rule)
whether 0.90 is reused or re-set per n
analysis.sd9Consequence: in the per-pair form, short-vs-long edges can remove a MEASURABLE survivor, which the ratified SD9 envelope assumes never happens (membership policy clause5: treatments may not retroactively remove a known measurable survivor); A2 outcomes would therefore no longer be provably preserved. Restricting B to short-vs-short pairs avoids this but leaves an uncalibrated gradation over the shortest texts.

C.summary: Documents with fewer than five canonical tokens are deterministically ineligible for SET_P and SET_R.

consequences.changesSd3Population: YES - SD3 draws "from the organisation acquired, policy-authorised, deduplicated pages" with "NO class filtering of any kind"; C removes a content-defined subset of that pool before ranking.
consequences.preservesSetPPrevalenceFaithfulness: NO - SET_P is the only prevalence-faithful stratum (SD11). Short pages exist in production and would be classified there; removing them changes the population G3 (precision) and G6 (needs-review) are estimated on, and short pages plausibly concentrate in particular page types (stubs, navigation, error-like pages), so the shift is not class-neutral. SD6 explicitly forbids filtering SET_P toward or away from hard negatives.

consequences.altersSd9Meaning: YES if left alone: SD9 counts post-SD7 pages with extractable text, and MIN_PAGES_PER_ORGANISATION = 4 is justified as the SET_R cap. Under C an organisation can be ACQUISITION_SUCCESSFUL with fewer than four SAMPLE-ELIGIBLE pages, so the justification breaks.

consequences.couldThatChangeA2Outcomes: NO for finalised statuses, provably: the ratified envelope lower bound already counts measurable (>=5-token) survivors only, so every finalised success had a measurable minimum >= 4, and every finalised failure had a maximum < 4 even with all short documents counted. recommendedMethodologyClassification.rationale: Option A changes no defined value, no population, no estimand and no acquisition generation, so a new major version or a new generation id would misdescribe it - a new generation id would wrongly imply a new acquisition cohort. It IS a methodology amendment (it decides a semantic question R3 left open), so it cannot be another operational owner record. "R4" in the additive form is the honest label: R3 bytes are never edited, the R4 record states only the amended clause, and it becomes operative only through a separate owner approval of its exact bytes.
recommendedMethodologyClassification.crossGenerationRequirement: Methodology V3 inherits R3 by exact SHA-256 and applies it "UNCHANGED, except the amendments listed". An R4 that named only V2 would leave Generation-2-carried slots of the same 110-slot cohort under the old SD7 branch. The R4 approval must therefore state explicitly that the amended SD7 clause applies identically to METHODOLOGY_V2_GEN1 and METHODOLOGY_V3_GEN2 slots. This is a scope statement inside the amendment, not a V3 amendment of reserves or continuity.

clauses.text: Scope is unchanged: the SD7 near-duplicate relation is evaluated WITHIN ONE ORGANISATION ONLY, over that organisation's distinct documents after exact duplicates are collapsed by documentSha256. No pair spanning two organisations is ever formed.

Canonical token sequence T(d): apply exactly the SD7 normalisation already in force - locale-independent lower-casing, trim, collapse every Unicode whitespace run to one U+0020 - then split on U+0020; an empty normalised text yields the EMPTY sequence (length 0). No stemming, no punctuation stripping, no accent removal, no Unicode canonical normalisation, no language-specific tokenisation.

Shingle-defined branch (|T(a)| >= 5 AND |T(b)| >= 5): unchanged byte-for-byte. The pair is a near duplicate iff |S(a) n S(b)| * 10 >= |S(a) u S(b)| * 9, where S is the set of overlapping 5-token shingles. NEAR_DUPLICATE_SHINGLE_SIZE = 5 and NEAR_DUPLICATE_JACCARD_THRESHOLD = 0.90 at-or-above inclusive are unchanged.

Short-text branch (|T(a)| < 5 OR |T(b)| < 5): the pair is a near duplicate iff T(a) and T(b) have the same length and are element-wise identical as strings; otherwise it is NOT a near duplicate. Because tokens contain no whitespace, this is equivalent to equality of the two normalised texts.

Zero tokens: the empty sequence equals only the empty sequence. Two zero-token documents are near duplicates of each other; a zero-token document is not a near duplicate of any document with one or more tokens. This clause does not change which documents reach SD7: the SD9 extractable-text rule (zero-character rows never enter SD7) is unchanged.

Symmetry: every verdict is symmetric in (a, b). On the short-text branch the relation is an equivalence, so short-text near-duplicate components are cliques; no edge ever joins a short document to a document with five or more tokens.

Survivors: unchanged. The K3 GREEDY_SAMPLE_RANK_SURVIVOR_WALK applies per sample: walk the sample's frozen order earliest to latest and keep a document iff it has no edge to a document already kept - the earlier by that sample's rank survives.
No new numeric parameter: no new threshold, n-gram size, similarity value or eligibility count is introduced. The number 5 continues only to mark where shingle Jaccard is defined.

Meaning: a short-text-branch edge means only "the same canonical text, counted once for SD7 exclusion". It is not semantic equivalence, not a class, not a label and not a statement about the organisation.

Flag: under this rule no pair is SD7_SHORT_TEXT_UNRESOLVED. A document with fewer than five canonical tokens remains recorded descriptively (token count, short-text branch) as evidence; it is neither excluded from the pre-SD7 population nor moved in any rank.

Application: one global rule, applied identically to every organisation of the 110-slot cohort, to Generation 1 and Generation 2 slots alike, and to DEV_TRAIN, DEV_CONFIRM and FINAL_HOLDOUT, with no reference to split, label, gold, model output, gate result, class balance or any observed effect of the rule.

Supersession: the rule supersedes, for the short-text branch only, the operational clauses listed in supersessionPlan; every other clause of every earlier record remains binding, and no earlier record is edited.
